trust_decision.summary: Any logged-in user's sendAsEmail subject/message is evaluated as Velocity; the only sandbox is a name denylist (string scan in Automation.forbidRuntimeUsage plus exact-name checks in ClassTool.newInstance/forName), and the fix widens the ClassTool denylist to ProcessBuilder and filters the attached-document dictionary to downloadable documents.

landing_point.why: The summary names the sendAsEmail template; this line is where the user's message goes into the Velocity engine.

fix_sites.entry_point: $ClassTool.newInstance(...) inside any Automation script; reached by GWT RPC DocumentService.sendAsEmail
fix_sites.module_kind: lower-level automation dictionary tool (core library, another module)

fix_sites.entry_point: $ClassTool.forName(...) inside any Automation script; reached by GWT RPC DocumentService.sendAsEmail
fix_sites.module_kind: lower-level automation dictionary tool (core library, another module)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: logicaldoc-core/src/main/java/com/logicaldoc/core/automation/ClassTool.java:43-81 (an @AutomationDictionary tool in logicaldoc-core, reflectively put into every script dictionary by Automation.prepareDictionary at logicaldoc-core/src/main/java/com/logicaldoc/core/automation/Automation.java:148-166)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: ClassTool is a documented general-purpose scripting utility used by admin automation (validators, initializers, dashlets, templates), so 'leave the tool alone and just stop evaluating or sanitize the email text in sendAsEmail' looks like a narrower and safer change.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The sendAsEmail subject/message are meant to be templates: legitimate $document/$documents/$sender/$downloadTicket references and dictionary tools must still render, and ClassTool.newInstance must still build com.logicaldoc.* tools with the short-name prefix fallback. Removing evaluation or blocking ClassTool outright breaks these.

attached doc ids the user may not download (filtered from the dictionary, fix.diff:49-58)

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is code injection (CWE-94); attachment permissions look like a neighbouring authorization feature, and the dictionary filter seems to cover 'the documents'.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, about 170 lines below the landing point (createAttachment at :1686-1718)

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Ticket mode is a separate send option (sendAsTicket), and ticket creation belongs to DocumentManager, so it looks out of scope.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Message templates stored by any session user through MessageService.saveTemplates are later evaluated by Automation (the sink-level denylist applies, but there is no author gate)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Templates are an admin settings feature and a stored, not direct, input; the email report never mentions them.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other file, same webapp package; sink reached through logicaldoc-core/src/main/java/com/logicaldoc/core/communication/MessageTemplate.java:79-81

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The string-scan denylist matches only 'java.lang.Runtime' and '.getRuntime'/'.runtime', not ProcessBuilder or split/concatenated names, so it disagrees with the ClassTool list.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Two denylists for one policy kept in two places; a maintainer updating one and forgetting the other is the exact history this fix shows.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Class objects (Paths, Math) and the Spring application Context are put straight into the dictionary, giving reflective reach that does not go through ClassTool.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Added for script convenience; a how-type sibling whose fix needs the dictionary producer understood, not the ClassTool check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The prefix fallback retries Class.forName with 'com.logicaldoc.' + name after the check; a planted normalization (trim/case) after the check would be a check-then-rename differential.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fallback already rewrites the name after the check; adding a normalization step there is a plausible refactor.
